q: Is the DSB-yield-per-Gy for p(66)/Be(40) fast neutrons in human lymphocytes energy-dependent within the neutron spectrum, i.e. does the mean neutron energy (nominally ~29 MeV for p(66)/Be(40)) systematically shift the induction curve compared to nearby neutron facilities (e.g. 14 MeV D-T, 62 MeV clinical proton-neutron secondary fields)?
basis: The paper reports only a single 'fast' neutron field, does not include the energy spectrum, and does not compare against other neutron facilities. Without the spectrum file, cross-facility comparison is impossible.
next_steps: Extract neutron energy spectrum from iThemba LABS dosimetry references [42] via literature review (Nolte et al., de Kock, etc.).; Cross-check against ICRU 63 / ICRU 95 neutron reference fields for p+Be systems.; Compare per-Gy DSB yield to published 14 MeV (JAERI, PTB) and 62 MeV (Louvain, HIT) lymphocyte gamma-H2AX datasets.

q: Is the RBE-vs-LET curve for fast-neutron-induced DSBs in lymphocytes reproducible across laboratories, given that this paper does not include a matched low-LET reference arm?
basis: The paper does not calculate an internal RBE; any RBE inference relies on cross-study low-LET baselines that may differ in donor pool, scoring method (manual vs Metafer), or fixation time.
next_steps: Assemble published low-LET (60Co, 6 MV X-ray, 250 kVp) gamma-H2AX per-cell foci-per-Gy in lymphocytes at the same 30-min post-IR time point.; Compute RBE_DSB = (foci/Gy)_neutron / (foci/Gy)_low-LET with donor-pool and scoring-method covariates.; Compare against DSB-RBE predicted by MCDS / PARTRAC given the p(66)/Be(40) spectrum.

q: Does the paper's ~40 % HDR-over-LDR DSB-yield effect translate to modern PBL biodosimetry protocols (dicentric assay, PCC, micronuclei), or is it a gamma-H2AX-specific phenomenon (e.g. attributable to foci merger / scoring saturation at high induction rates)?
basis: The paper reports one endpoint (gamma-H2AX foci). Whether the dose-rate effect at high LET has the same magnitude for chromosomal aberrations (dicentrics, translocations) --- the actual clinical biodosimetry endpoints --- is not tested here.
next_steps: Meta-analyse published dicentric / micronucleus yields for fast neutrons at HDR vs LDR in lymphocytes.; If per-cell foci CSV becomes available (currently not deposited), estimate foci-merger correction using published spatial-statistics models (Neumaier et al., Herr et al.).; Test whether the K-coefficient peak at 0.250 Gy reflects a scoring-saturation artifact rather than biology.

q: What is the DSB-induction and DSB-repair response of lymphocytes to mixed neutron+gamma fields (as encountered clinically in BNCT, in reactor incidents, and in criticality accidents), and can it be predicted linearly from the pure-neutron (this paper) plus pure-gamma responses?
basis: The paper studies a single pure-neutron field. Real high-LET exposures (BNCT, reactor, criticality) always include a substantial gamma component, and the interaction (super-additive? synergistic on repair kinetics?) is unresolved.
next_steps: Search for lymphocyte gamma-H2AX studies in BNCT beams (Kyoto, Petten, Argentina) reporting neutron-fraction-resolved DSB yields.; If pure-gamma HDR/LDR data on the same iThemba cohort exist, compute (neutron+gamma) - predicted-additive to test super-additivity.; Model a mixed-field DSB yield using MCDS with paired neutron and gamma track structure and compare to any available mixed-field data.

q: Can the ~40 % HDR-over-LDR DSB-yield effect and the (LDR > HDR) repair-half-life ordering be coupled to a cytogenetic aberration model (e.g. the two-lesion / BLE / Sachs-Hlatky repair-misrepair framework) to predict dicentric yield at the same dose rates?
basis: The paper stops at DSB yield and repair kinetics; it does not link these to chromosomal aberration formation, which is the endpoint that actually matters for biodosimetry and risk estimation.
next_steps: Parameterise a two-lesion kinetic (TLK) or Sachs-Rossi model with the paper's fitted induction and repair rates.; Predict per-dose dicentric yield at HDR vs LDR from the coupled model.; Compare against published dicentric-yield-vs-dose curves for fast neutrons in lymphocytes (Vral, IAEA).
